o: I stalo se jednoho čtvrtku, kdy londýnské zoo bylo obecenstvu uzavřeno, že pan Thomas Greggs, hlídač v pavilonu ještěrů, čistil nádrže a terária svých svěřenců.
t: It happened one Thursday, when the London Zoo was closed to the public, that Mr Thomas Greggs, the keeper in the reptile house, was cleaning the tanks and terrariums of his charges.

o: Byl sám a sám v oddílu mloků, kde byl vystaven velemlok japonský, americký hellbendr, Andrias Scheuchzeri a množství drobných čolků, mločíků, axolotlů, ouhoříků, surýnů a macarátů, žebrovníků i žábronošů.
t: He was alone in the newt section, where a Japanese giant salamander was on display, along with the American hellbender, Andrias Scheuchzeri, and a number of small newts, olms, axolotls, sirens, surinam toads and macropods, mudpuppies and mud-fish.

o: Pan Greggs se oháněl hadrem a koštětem, pískaje si Annie Laurie; a najednou někdo za ním skřehotavě povídá.
t: Mr Greggs was waving a cloth and a broom, whistling Annie Laurie to himself; and suddenly someone behind him said in a croaky voice.

o: Pan Thomas Greggs se ohlédl, ale nikdo tam nebyl; jen hellbendr mlaskal ve svém bahně a ten velký černý mlok, ten Andrias, se opíral předními tlapkami o kraj nádrže a kroutil trupem.
t: Mr Thomas Greggs looked around, but no one was there; only the hellbender splashed in its mud, and the big black newt, that Andrias, propped itself up on its forefeet at the edge of the tank and wriggled its body.

o: Něco se mi zdálo, mínil pan Greggs a metl dál podlahu, až to svištělo.
t: Something seemed to me to be off, thought Mr Greggs, and he went on sweeping the floor until it squeaked.
"Look here, newt," a voice said behind him.

o: Pan Greggs se rychle otočil; ten černý mlok, ten Andrias, se na něho díval, mrkaje spodními víčky.
t: Mr Greggs turned quickly; the black newt, that Andrias, was looking at him, blinking with its lower lids.

o: „Brr, ten je ošklivý,“ řekl najednou mlok.
t: "Ugh, that one is ugly," said the newt suddenly.
"Come away from there, darling."
Mr. Greggs opened his mouth in astonishment. "What?"
"He doesn't bite?" squeaked the newt.

o: „Ty… ty umíš mluvit?“ koktal pan Greggs, nevěře svým smyslům.
t: "You... you can speak?" stammered Mr. Greggs, not believing his own senses.

o: „Já se ho bojím,“ vyrazil ze sebe mlok. „Mami, co žere?“
t: "I'm afraid of him," the newt blurted out. "Mommy, what's he eating?"

o: „Řekni dobrý den,“ řekl užaslý pan Greggs.
t: "Say good day," said Mr. Greggs, astounded.
The newt wriggled his body.
"Good day," he squeaked.
"Good day. Good day."
May I give him a cake?"

o: Pan Greggs sáhl zmateně do kapsy a vytáhl kousek housky. „Na, tumáš.“
t: Mr. Greggs fumbled into his pocket and pulled out a bit of bread. "Here, take it."

o: Mlok vzal housku do tlapky a počal ji okusovat.
t: The newt took the bread in his little paw and began to nibble at it.
"Look at that, newt," he croaked contentedly.
"Daddy, why is he so black?"

o: Náhle se ponořil do vody a vystrčil jen hlavu.
t: He suddenly ducked under the water, sticking out only his head.
"Why is he in the water?"
Why? Huh, that one is ugly!"

o: Pan Thomas Greggs se škrábal překvapením v týle.
t: Mr. Thomas Greggs scratched the back of his head in surprise.

o: Aha, to on opakuje, co tady slyší od lidí.
t: Ah, he's repeating what he hears people say here.
"Say Greggs," he tried.
"Say Greggs," the newt repeated.
“Mr Thomas Greggs.”
“Mr Thomas Greggs.”
“Good day, sir.”
“Good day, sir.
Good day. Good day, sir.”

o: Zdálo se, že se mlok nemůže řeči nabažit; ale Greggs už nevěděl, co by mu povídal; pan Thomas Greggs nebyl muž příliš výmluvný.
t: It seemed the newt could not be got to say more; but Greggs no longer knew what to say to him; Mr Thomas Greggs was not a very talkative man.

o: „Tak teď drž hubu,“ řekl, „a až budu hotov, budu tě učit mluvit.“
t: “Now just keep your mouth shut,” he said, “and when I’m done, I’ll teach you to speak.”
“Now just keep your mouth shut,” the newt muttered.
“Good day, sir.
I’ll teach you to speak.”

o: Jenže ředitelství zoo nevidělo rádo, když hlídači učili svá zvířata nějakým kouskům; něco jiného je slon, ale ostatní zvířata tu jsou pro poučení, a ne aby provozovala něco jako cirkus.
t: The zoo management, however, did not care for the keepers teaching their animals little tricks; an elephant is one thing, but the other animals are here for instruction, not for putting on something like a circus.

o: Proto pan Greggs trávil svůj čas v oddělení mloků víceméně potají, když tam už nikdo nebyl.
t: So Greggs spent his time in the newt department more or less in secret, when no one else was there.

o: Jelikož byl vdovec, nedivil se nikdo jeho samotaření v pavilonu ještěrů.
t: Since he was a widower, no one wondered at his solitary hours in the reptile house.

o: Každý člověk má své zvláštní záliby.
t: Every man has his peculiar tastes.

o: Ostatně do oddělení mloků chodilo málo lidí; to spíš krokodýl se těšil obecné popularitě, ale Andrias Scheuchzeri trávil své dny v poměrné samotě.
t: Besides, few people came to the newt department; it was rather the crocodile who enjoyed general popularity, while Andrias Scheuchzeri spent his days in relative solitude.

o: Jednou, když se už šeřilo a pavilony se zavíraly, procházel ředitel zoo sir Charles Wiggam některými odděleními, aby se přesvědčil, je-li všechno v pořádku.
t: Once, when it was already growing dark and the pavilions were closing, the zoo director, Sir Charles Wiggam, walked through some of the departments to make sure everything was in order.

o: Když šel oddílem mloků, zašplounalo to v jedné nádrži a někdo skřehotavě řekl: „Dobrý večer, pane.“
t: As he passed through the newt section, something splashed in one of the tanks and a voice said in a shrill tone: “Good evening, sir.”

o: „Dobrý večer,“ odpověděl ředitel překvapeně. „Kdo je tam?“
t: “Good evening,” the director replied, surprised. “Who’s there?”
“Excuse me, sir,” said the shrill voice.
“That’s not Mr Greggs.”
“Who’s there?” the director repeated.
“Andy. Andrew Scheuchzer.”

o: Sir Charles šel blíž k nádrži.
t: Sir Charles walked closer to the pond.

o: Seděl tam jenom vztyčený a nehybný mlok.
t: Only a newt sat there, upright and motionless.
"Who was talking?"
"Andy, sir," said the newt. "Who are you?"
"Wiggam," Sir Charles blurted out, astounded.

o: „Těší mě,“ děl Andrias zdvořile. „Jak se máte?“
t: "Delighted to meet you," said Andrias politely. "How are you?"
"Devil take it," roared Sir Charles, "Greggs!"

o: Mlok sebou mýkl a schoval se střelhbitě ve vodě.
t: The newt flicked itself and swiftly hid in the water.

o: Do dveří vrazil Mr Thomas Greggs, udýchaný a znepokojený. „Prosím, pane?“
t: Mr Thomas Greggs burst through the door, breathless and alarmed. "You called, sir?"

o: „Greggsi, co to znamená?“ spustil sir Charles.
t: "Greggs, what is the meaning of this?" Sir Charles demanded.

o: „Stalo se něco, pane?“ koktal pan Greggs nejistě.
t: "Has something happened, sir?" Mr Greggs stammered uncertainly.
"This animal is talking!"
"I beg your pardon, sir," said Mr Greggs, crushed.
"You mustn't do that, Andy.

o: Říkal jsem vám tisíckrát, že nemáte obtěžovat lidi svým povídáním.
t: I have told you a thousand times that you must not bother people with your talking.

o: – Prosím za prominutí, pane, víckrát se to nestane.“
t: "I beg your pardon, sir; it won't happen again."

o: „To vy jste naučil toho mloka mluvit?“
t: "Did you teach that newt to speak?"

o: „Ale on začal, pane,“ hájil se Greggs.
t: "But he started it, sir," Greggs defended himself.

o: „Doufám, že se to nebude opakovat, Greggsi,“ řekl přísně sir Charles.
t: "I hope it won't happen again, Greggs," said Sir Charles sternly.
"I'll keep an eye on you."

o: Po nějaké době seděl sir Charles s profesorem Petrovem a hovořili o takzvané zvířecí inteligenci, o podmíněných reflexech a o tom, jak populární názory přeceňují rozumovou činnost zvířat.
t: After a while Sir Charles was sitting with Professor Petrov, and they were talking about so-called animal intelligence, about conditioned reflexes, and about how popular opinion overrates the mental activity of animals.

o: Profesor Petrov vyslovil své pochybnosti o elberfeldských koních, kteří prý dovedli nejen počítat, ale i umocňovat a odmocňovat; vždyť ani normální, vzdělaný člověk neumí odmocňovat, řekl veliký učenec.
t: Professor Petrov voiced his doubts about the Elberfeld horses, which were said to be able not only to count but also to square and take square roots; after all, said the great scholar, not even a normal, educated human being can take square roots.

o: Sir Charles si vzpomněl na Greggsova mluvícího mloka.
t: Sir Charles remembered Greggs's talking newt.

o: „Já tady mám mloka,“ začal váhavě, „je to ten známý Andrias Scheuchzeri; a ten se naučil mluvit jako papoušek.“
t: "I have a newt here," he began hesitantly, "the famous Andrias Scheuchzeri; and he has learned to talk like a parrot."
"Impossible," said the scholar.
"Newts have a tongue that is not attached, after all."

o: „Tak se pojďte podívat,“ řekl sir Charles.
t: "Then come and have a look," said Sir Charles.

o: „Dnes je den čištění, tak tam nebude plno lidí.“ A šli.
t: "Today is cleaning day, so there won't be many people there." And they went.

o: U vchodu k mlokům se sir Charles zastavil.
t: At the entrance to the newts Sir Charles stopped.

o: Zvnitřku bylo slyšet škrabot koštěte a jednotvárný hlas, který cosi slabikoval.
t: From within came the scratching of a broom and a monotonous voice that was syllableing something.
"Wait," whispered Sir Charles.

o: „Jsou na Martu lidé?“ slabikoval jednotvárný hlas. „Mám to číst?“
t: "Are there people at Marta?" the monotonous voice syllableed. "Am I to read?"
"Something else, Andy," answered a second voice.

o: „Zvítězí v letošním derby Pelham-Beauty nebo Gobernador?“
t: "Will Pelham-Beauty or Gobernador win in this year's Derby?"
"Pelham-Beauty," said the second voice. "But read."
Sir Charles quietly opened the door.

o: Pan Thomas Greggs zametal koštětem podlahu; a v rybníčku s mořskou vodou seděl Andrias Scheuchzeri a pomalu, skřehotavě slabikoval z večerních novin, které držel v předních tlapkách.
t: Mr Thomas Greggs was sweeping the floor with a broom; and in the pond of seawater sat Andrias Scheuchzeri, slowly and raspingly syllableing out the evening news, which he held in his front flippers.
"Greggs," called Sir Charles.

o: Mlok sebou hodil a zmizel pod vodou.
t: The newt flung himself forward and vanished under the water.

o: Mr Greggs upustil leknutím koště. „Ano, pane?“
t: Mr Greggs dropped the broom in fright. "Yes, sir?"

o: „Prosím za prominutí, pane,“ koktal nešťastný Greggs.
t: "Beg your pardon, sir," stammered the unfortunate Greggs.
"Andy reads to me while I sweep.

o: A když zametá on, čtu zase já jemu.“
t: And when he sweeps, I read to him in turn."
"Who taught him that?"
"He picked it up on his own, sir.

o: Já… já mu dávám své noviny, aby tolik nemluvil.
t: I... I give him my newspapers, so that he doesn't talk so much.
He kept on talking, sir.

o: Myslel jsem tedy, aby se aspoň naučil mluvit vzdělaně –“
t: So I thought he might at least learn to speak properly -"
"Andy," called Sir Wiggam.

o: Z vody se vynořila černá hlava.
t: A black head rose out of the water.
"Yes, sir," croaked a voice.

o: „Přišel se na tebe podívat profesor Petrov.“
t: "Professor Petrov has come to see you."
I am Andy Scheuchzer."

o: „Jak to víš, že se jmenuješ Andrias Scheuchzeri?“
t: "How do you know your name is Andrias Scheuchzer?"
"I have it written down here, sir.
Andreas Scheuchzer. Gilbert Islands."
"And do you read the papers often?"
"Yes, sir. Every day, sir."
"And what interests you most in them?"
"Courtrooms, horse races, football -"
"Have you ever seen a dugout?"
"Then why do you read it?"
"Because it's in the papers, sir."
"Politics doesn't interest you?"
"No, sir. Will there be a war?"
"Nobody knows that, Andy."

o: „Německo buduje nový typ ponorek,“ řekl Andy starostlivě.
t: "Germany is building a new type of submarine," Andy said solicitously.

o: „Paprsky smrti mohou obrátit celé pevniny v poušť.“
t: "Death rays could turn whole continents into desert."

o: „Tos četl v novinách, ne?“ ptal se sir Charles.
t: "You read that in the papers, didn't you?" asked Sir Charles.

o: „Ano, pane. Zvítězí v letošním derby Pelham-Beauty nebo Gobernador?“
t: "Yes, sir. Will Pelham-Beauty or Gobernador win the Derby this year?"
"What do you think, Andy?"

o: „Gobernador, pane; ale pan Greggs myslí, že Pelham-Beauty.“
t: "Gobernador, sir; but Mr. Greggs thinks Pelham-Beauty."
Andy shook his head.
"Buy English goods, sir.
Snider's boots are the best.

o: Máte už nový šesticylindr Tancred Junior?
t: Have you got the new six-cylinder Tancred Junior yet?
Fast, cheap, elegant."
"Thanks, Andy. That's enough."

o: „Která filmová umělkyně se vám nejvíc líbí?“
t: "Which film actress do you like best?"

o: Profesor Petrov naježil vlasy i vousy.
t: Professor Petrov ran his fingers through his hair and whiskers.

o: „Promiňte, sir Charles,“ bručel, „ale já už musím jít.“
t: "Sorry, Sir Charles," he muttered, "but I really must go."
"Very well, let's go."

o: Andy, měl bys něco proti tomu, kdybych k tobě poslal několik učených pánů?
t: Andy, would you have any objection if I sent a few learned gentlemen to you?

o: Myslím, že by si s tebou rádi promluvili.“
t: I think they would be glad to talk with you."
"It will be a pleasure, sir," squeaked the newt.
"Goodbye, Sir Charles.
Goodbye, Professor."

o: Profesor Petrov běžel, podrážděně frkaje a brumlaje.
t: Professor Petrov trotted along, grumbling and muttering irritably.

o: „Odpusťte, sir Charles,“ řekl konečně, „ale nemohl byste mně ukázat nějaké zvíře, které nečte noviny?“
t: "Excuse me, Sir Charles," he said at last, "but couldn't you show me some animal that doesn't read the newspapers?"

o: Ti učení páni, to byli sir Bertram, D. M., profesor Ebbigham, sir Oliver Dodge, Julian Foxley a jiní.
t: Those learned gentlemen were Sir Bertram, D. M., Professor Ebbigham, Sir Oliver Dodge, Julian Foxley, and others.

o: Citujeme část protokolu jejich pokusu s Andriasem Scheuchzeri.
t: We quote part of the record of their experiment with Andrias Scheuchzeri.
What is your name?
Ans.: Andrew Scheuchzer.
Do you want to look young?
Wear the Libella snuff-box.
What day of the month is it?
Fine weather, sir.

o: Tuto sobotu poběží v Epsomu Gibraltar.
t: Gibraltar will race at Epsom this Saturday.
How much is three times five?
How much is seventeen times twenty-nine?

o: Nechte nás, abychom se ptali, Andrew.
t: Let us ask you, Andrew.
Name us some English rivers.
You don't know any others, do you?
Who rules England?

o: Odp.: King George. God bless him.
t: A: King George. God bless him.
Who is the greatest English writer?
Have you read anything by him?

o: Odp.: Ne. Jak se vám líbí Mae West?
t: A: No. How do you like Mae West?

o: My se raději budeme ptát vás, Andy.
t: We'd rather ask you, Andy.
What do you know about English history?
A: Henry the Eighth.
A: The best film of recent years.
A wonderful adventure. A magnificent show.
Have you seen it?
Do you want to get to know England?
Buy a Ford Baby.

o: Co byste nejvíc chtěl vidět, Andy?
t: What would you most like to see, Andy?
A: The Cambridge–Oxford race, sir.
How many parts of the world are there?

o: Velmi dobře. A které to jsou?
t: Very good. And which ones are they?
A: England and the others.
Which are the others?

o: Odp.: To jsou bolševici a Němci. A Itálie.
t: A: Those are the Bolsheviks and the Germans. And Italy.
Where are the Gilberts?

o: Odp.: V Anglii, Anglie si nebude vázat ruce na pevnině.
t: A: In England. England will not tie its hands on the continent.
England needs ten thousand aircraft.
Visit the coast of southern England.

o: Smíme se podívat na váš jazyk, Andy?
t: May we have a look at your language, Andy?
Brush your teeth with Flit toothpaste.

o: Je úsporná, je nejlepší, je anglická.
t: It is economical, it is the best, it is English.
Do you want to have fresh breath?
Use Flit toothpaste.
Thank you, that will do.
And now tell us, Andy…

o: A tak dále. Protokol rozmluvy s Andriasem Scheuchzeri čítal šestnáct plných stran a byl uveřejněn v The Natural Science.
t: And so on. The record of the conversation with Andrias Scheuchzeri ran to sixteen full pages and was published in The Natural Science.

o: Na konci protokolu shrnula odborná komise výsledky svého pokusu takto.
t: At the end of the record, the commission of experts summarized the results of its experiment as follows.

o: 1. Andrias Scheuchzeri, mlok chovaný v londýnském zoo, dovede mluvit, byť poněkud skřehotavě; disponuje asi čtyřmi sty slovy; říká jen to, co slyšel nebo četl.
t: 1. Andrias Scheuchzeri, a newt kept in the London zoo, can speak, though somewhat hoarsely; he has about four hundred words at his disposal; he says only what he has heard or read.

o: O samostatném myšlení u něho nelze ovšem mluvit.
t: Independent thinking, however, cannot be attributed to him.

o: Jeho jazyk je dosti pohyblivý; hlasivky jsme za daných okolností nemohli blíže zkoumat.
t: His tongue is fairly mobile; under the given circumstances we were unable to examine his vocal cords more closely.

o: 2. Týž mlok dovede číst, ale jenom večerníky novin.
t: 2. The same newt can read, but only the evening editions of newspapers.

o: Zajímá se o tytéž věci jako průměrný Angličan a reaguje na ně podobným způsobem, to jest ve směru ustálených, obecných názorů.
t: He is interested in the same things as the average Englishman and reacts to them in a similar way, that is, in terms of established, general opinions.

o: Jeho duševní život – pokud lze o nějakém mluvit – pozůstává právě z představ a mínění toho času běžných.
t: His mental life—if one can speak of it at all—consists precisely of the ideas and opinions common to his time.

o: 3. Jeho inteligenci není naprosto třeba přeceňovat, neboť v žádném ohledu nepřekračuje inteligenci průměrného člověka našich dnů.
t: 3. His intelligence need by no means be overrated, for in no respect does it surpass the intelligence of the average person of our days.

o: Přes tento střízlivý úsudek odborníků se Mluvící Mlok stal senzací londýnské zoo.
t: Despite this sober judgment of experts, the Talking Mole became a sensation at the London zoo.

o: Miláček Andy byl obležen lidmi, kteří s ním chtěli zapříst hovor o všem možném, počínajíc počasím a končíc hospodářskou krizí a politickou situací.
t: The darling Andy was surrounded by people who wanted to chat with him about everything possible, starting with the weather and ending with the economic crisis and the political situation.

o: Přitom dostával od svých návštěvníků tolik čokolády a bonbonů, že těžce ochuravěl žaludečním a střevním katarem.
t: Meanwhile he was receiving so much chocolate and sweets from his visitors that he fell gravely ill with gastric and intestinal catarrh.

o: Oddělení mloků muselo být konečně zavřeno, ale bylo už pozdě; Andrias Scheuchzeri, řečený Andy, zašel na následky své popularity.
t: The mole exhibit finally had to be closed, but it was already too late; Andrias Scheuchzeri, called Andy, died of the consequences of his popularity.

o: Jak vidět, demoralizuje sláva i mloky.
t: As you can see, fame demoralizes even moles.
